questions.stem: Cystic fibrosis is caused by which type of allele?
questions.explanation: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a recessive allele. This means a person must inherit two copies of the recessive allele (one from each parent) to be affected. Carriers (heterozygous) have one copy but do not show symptoms.

questions.stem: What are the main symptoms of cystic fibrosis?

options.text: Thick, sticky mucus in the lungs and digestive system

questions.explanation: Cystic fibrosis causes the production of thick, sticky mucus that blocks the airways and pancreatic ducts. This leads to breathing difficulties, frequent chest infections, and problems with digestion.

questions.stem: Sickle cell disease is caused by a mutation in the gene coding for which protein?
questions.explanation: Sickle cell disease is caused by a mutation in the gene that codes for haemoglobin. The abnormal haemoglobin causes red blood cells to become rigid and sickle-shaped, blocking blood vessels and reducing oxygen delivery.

questions.stem: Two parents who are both carriers of cystic fibrosis have a child. What is the probability that the child will have cystic fibrosis?
questions.explanation: Both parents are carriers (Cc). From a Cc x Cc cross: CC, Cc, Cc, cc. Only cc (1 in 4, or 25%) will have cystic fibrosis. There is a 2 in 4 chance of being a carrier and 1 in 4 chance of being unaffected and not a carrier.

questions.stem: Huntington's disease differs from cystic fibrosis because it is caused by:

options.text: A sex-linked allele on the X chromosome

questions.explanation: Huntington's disease is caused by a dominant allele, meaning only one copy is needed to cause the disorder. This is different from cystic fibrosis, which requires two recessive alleles. Huntington's symptoms typically appear in middle age.

options.text: A treatment that cures genetic disorders
A way to prevent mutations from occurring
A method of changing a person's DNA
Testing to determine if a person carries alleles for a genetic disorder

questions.explanation: Genetic screening involves testing individuals to find out if they carry alleles for particular genetic disorders. This helps people make informed decisions about having children and allows early detection of conditions.

questions.stem: Why might carriers of the sickle cell allele have an advantage in regions where malaria is common?

options.text: Because carriers have some resistance to malaria
Because they are immune to all diseases
Because carriers have stronger immune systems overall
Because the malaria parasite cannot survive in their blood at all

questions.explanation: Carriers of the sickle cell allele (heterozygous) have some protection against malaria because the malaria parasite finds it harder to survive in their red blood cells. This is why the sickle cell allele is more common in malaria-affected regions.
